This is the markdown file in which we take the df with the first observation from the dm_code list, the lgycaemic_test_code list, the dm_drugs list and the HES DM code list and filter down to data, for each patid for those with single patids or individual_id for those with multiple patids, which does reliable signify diabetes.

###load data and libraries
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
options(scipen = 999)
```

# Generic functions

```{r}
#filtering according to whether an individual has or doesn't have more than 1 patid
single <- function(df){df %>% filter(is.na(individual_id))}
multiple <- function(df){df %>% filter(!is.na(individual_id))}

#propagating relevant data across all the patids of a given individual
fill_columns <- function(df, ...) {
  df %>% 
    left_join(all_pats, by = "individual_id") %>%
    group_by(individual_id) %>%
    fill(..., .direction = "downup") %>%
    ungroup()
}

#finding the earliest date across events for all an individual's patids, taking into account some or none of them may have had it (avoids error messages because of NAs)
safe_min <- function(x) if (all(is.na(x))) NA_Date_ else min(x, na.rm=TRUE)

#filter down to earliest obsdate per patid or individual_id
obsdate_single_fun <- function(df){df %>% group_by(patid) %>% slice_min(obsdate) %>% slice(1) %>% ungroup()}
obsdate_multiple_fun <- function(df){df %>% group_by(individual_id) %>% slice_min(obsdate) %>% slice(1) %>% ungroup()}

```

now load code lists and data. Note the code lists are more for reference. Generally it is assumed that the observations for those codes have been compounded into the observation files below by something like an inner_join to the observation list
```{r}
#medcodes
setwd("YOUR DIRECTORY")
dm_code <-read.delim("dm_code.txt", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
dm_drugs <- read.delim("dm_drugs.txt", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
dm_ICD <- read.delim("dm_ICD10_code.txt", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
gly_code <- read.delim("glycaemic_test_code.txt", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
gdm_code <- read.delim("gdm_code.txt", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
all_pregnancy_code <- read.delim("all_pregnancy_code.txt", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
ndh_code <- read.delim("ndh_code.txt", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
PCOS_code <- read.delim("pcos_code.txt", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)

metformin_code <- dm_drugs %>% 
  filter(is.na(priority_1)&is.na(priority_2)) 

insulin_code <- dm_drugs %>% 
  filter(!is.na(priority_2))

priority_1 <- dm_drugs %>% 
  filter(!is.na(priority_1))

#now load all your observation files - eg with read.delim if you have them as .txt or readRDS if saved as RDS files: you will need
first_obs_gly_drug_HES  #df contianing all first dates
all_pats  #all patids with adjoining individual_ids for patients that have more than one patid
all_dm_drugs               #all dm drug records for entire cohort
all_pcos_obs            #all pcos records for entire cohort
diagnostic_gly_obs       #all glycaemic tests meeting diagnostic criteria for diabetes for entire cohort
all_pregnancy_obs_update # all pregnancy observations, with delivery flags
all_dm_obs #all dm observations
ndh_obs #all ndh observations
delivery_obs #all delivery observations
normo #all observations of glycaemic tests NOT meeting the threshold for DM

#made from 5_pregnancy.rmd
valid_gdm_obs_multiple #valid gdm observations for those with multiple patids
valid_gdm_obs_single  #valid gdm observations for those with single patids
all_deliveries_single #all deliveries for those with single patids
all_deliveries_multiple #all deliveries for those with multiple patids
total_gdm_single_deliveries_slimmed #all GDM deliveries for those with single patids
total_gdm_multiple_deliveries_slimmed #all GDM deliveries for those with multiple patids

#ensure that all dfs have the indvidual_id colums
diagnostic_gly_obs <- diagnostic_gly_obs %>% 
  left_join(all_pats, by = "patid")

all_dm_obs <-all_dm_obs %>%
left_join(all_pats, by = "patid")

all_pcos_obs <- all_pcos_obs %>% 
  left_join(all_pats, by = "patid")

all_dm_drugs <- all_dm_drugs %>% 
  left_join(all_pats, by = "patid")

all_pregnancy_obs_update <- all_pregnancy_obs_update%>% 
  left_join(all_pats, by = "patid")

ndh_obs <- ndh_obs %>% 
  left_join(all_pats, by = "patid")

normo <- normo %>%  
  left_join(all_pats, by = "patid")

#propagate delivery dates to all relevant Patids for those with multiple patids
total_gdm_multiple_deliveries_slimmed <- total_gdm_multiple_deliveries_slimmed %>% 
  fill_columns() ## expect many-to-many warning
  
all_deliveries_multiple <- all_deliveries_multiple %>%
    fill_columns()#expect many to many

#this just narrows all_pats down to patids for individuals with multiple patids
all_pats <- multiple(first_obs_gly_drug_HES) %>% 
  distinct(patid, individual_id)

#number of distinct individuals with multiple patids
n_distinct(all_pats$individual_id)
```


#now for update 1: 
first identify subjects whose ddd is clearly erroneous (ie prior to or in year of birth)

```{r}
dodgy_ddd <- first_obs_gly_drug_HES %>% 
  filter(year(ddd)<=yob) %>% 
  select(patid, yob)

```

then get all their DM obs

```{r}
dodgy_ddd_all_obs <- all_dm_obs %>% 
  inner_join(dodgy_ddd, by = "patid")
```

now filter out any rows that are not helpful

```{r}
dodgy_ddd_next_ddd <- dodgy_ddd_all_obs %>% 
   mutate(
    obsdate = case_when(
      twelve_month_rev==1~obsdate %m-% years(1),
      six_month==1~obsdate %m-% days(182),
      three_month==1~obsdate %m-% days(91),
      TRUE~obsdate
    )) %>% 
    filter(year(obsdate)>yob) %>% ##ie erroneous date
  group_by(patid) %>%   
  filter(obsdate==min(obsdate)) %>% 
  ungroup() 

n_distinct(dodgy_ddd_next_ddd$patid) #4308
```

now prioritise as previously to get the most useful row of those on the next valid observation date

```{r}
prioritise_fun <- function(df){
  df %>% 
    group_by(patid) %>% 
    slice(
      if(any(!is.na(twelve_month_rev))){
        which(!is.na(twelve_month_rev))[1]
      }else if(any(!is.na(six_month))){
        which(!is.na(six_month))[1]
      }else if(any(!is.na(three_month))) {
        which(!is.na(three_month))[1]
      }else if(any(!is.na(unambiguous))) {
        which(!is.na(unambiguous))[1]
      }else{
        1
      }
    )
}
```

now filter down to single row per patient - should be 4849 patids

```{r}
dodgy_ddd_next_ddd <- prioritise_fun(dodgy_ddd_next_ddd) %>% 
  select(-value, -six_month, -three_month, -twelve_month_rev, -medcodeid, -possible_gdm, - unambiguous)
```

look at subjects who were diagnosed within 2 years of birth because
infant diabetes is so rare - 26 such patients

```{r}
filtered <- dodgy_ddd_next_ddd %>% 
  filter(year(obsdate)<=yob +2) 
```

look at all the obs for these few patids (in our case it was 38), and pick appropriate date
according to criteria broadly logic is if type 2 diabetes → next date
likely erroneous (type 2 is not infant diabetes) so use date after
that - if type 1 diabetes, more likely to be believable (unless datae
01 - 01 format) - if unclear whether type 1 or type 2, if significant
gap between the date and then next date after that, more likely
erroneous so need to adjust - wary of dates in 01-01 format create a
text file alongside called adjust_ddd with the outcome of the decision,
any new ddd and the patid

log these in a text file (in our case called adjust_ddd.txt) that we will load later, and create a new variable ddd-readjusted with the appropriate diabetes diagnosis date

```{r}
filtered_obs <- dodgy_ddd_all_obs %>% 
  filter(patid %in% filtered$patid)
```

now just look at impossible dates related to xprert referral pre 2000 (XPERT program did not exist before then)

```{r}

faulty_xpert <- first_obs_gly_drug_HES%>% 
  filter(ddd< as.Date("2000-01-01")) %>% 
  filter(grepl("xpert", diagnosis, ignore.case = TRUE))

dodgy_xpert_obs <- all_dm_obs %>% inner_join(faulty_xpert, by = "patid")
```


look through dodgy_xpert_obs and add to the updates from the review of filtered obs -> update adjusted_ddd

#load adjusted dates from text file prepared whilst review these dates

```{r}  

setwd("YOUR DIRECTORY")
adjusted_ddd <- read.delim("adjust_ddd.txt", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
adjusted_ddd$patid <- as.character(adjusted_ddd$patid)
```

select patients that need an update

```{r}
selected_adjusted_ddd <- adjusted_ddd %>% 
  filter(is.na(keep)) %>% 
  select(-keep)
selected_adjusted_ddd$ddd_readjusted <- as.Date(selected_adjusted_ddd$ddd_readjusted)
selected_adjusted_ddd$patid <- as.character(selected_adjusted_ddd$patid)
```

now join onto dodgy_ddd_next_date to replace previous dates

```{r}
dodgy_ddd_next_ddd <- dodgy_ddd_next_ddd %>% 
  left_join(selected_adjusted_ddd %>%  select(patid, ddd_readjusted, diagnosis_readjusted), by = "patid") %>% 
  mutate(obsdate = coalesce(ddd_readjusted, obsdate),
         Term = coalesce(diagnosis_readjusted, Term)) %>% 
  select(-diagnosis_readjusted, -ddd_readjusted, -yob)

```

note there may be some patids that don't have another useful obsdate, flag
these so that we know whose ddd needs to be removed

```{r}
patids_no_useful_date <- dodgy_ddd %>% 
  filter(!patid %in% dodgy_ddd_next_ddd$patid) %>% 
  mutate(no_useful_ddd = 1) %>% 
  select(-yob)
```

Now adjust the dates in first_update1_filter1 and call it update2, and also remove the ddd for the patids identified as not having a useful later date

```{r}
first_update1<- first_obs_gly_drug_HES %>% 
  left_join(dodgy_ddd_next_ddd %>% select(patid, obsdate, Term), by = "patid") %>% 
  mutate(ddd = if_else(!is.na(obsdate), obsdate, ddd),
         diagnosis = if_else(!is.na(Term), Term, diagnosis)) %>% 
  left_join(patids_no_useful_date, by = "patid") %>% #then adjust for those 8 patients
  mutate(ddd = if_else(!is.na(no_useful_ddd),NA, ddd),
         diagnosis = if_else(!is.na(no_useful_ddd), NA, diagnosis)) %>% 
  select(-obsdate, -Term, -no_useful_ddd) %>% 
  distinct() ##unclear why but a duplicate row is introduced here so distinct removes it

```
#now work on update 2 - updating the glycaemic tests with erronous dates

Find patids with dody gly_date (ie on or before their year of birth)
and get all their glycaemic data

```{r}
dodgy_gly <- first_update1 %>% 
  filter(year(gly_date)<=yob) %>% 
  select(patid, individual_id, yob)


dodgy_gly_obs <-diagnostic_gly_obs %>% 
    inner_join(dodgy_gly %>% select(patid, yob), by = "patid")

n_distinct(dodgy_gly_obs$patid) 
```

now find the next date per patid and relabel columns so as to avoid
confusion when left_joining to first_update2

```{r}
dodgy_gly_next_earliest <- dodgy_gly_obs%>% 
  filter(year(obsdate)>yob) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  filter(obsdate == min(obsdate)) %>% 
  arrange(index) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(gly_term_adjusted = Term) %>% 
  rename(gly_date_adjusted = obsdate) %>% 
  rename(value_adjusted = value) 
```
Here it is also now necessary to find the next earliest gly_date after the earliest for all subjects.  All patients with diabetes SHOULD have a second confirmatory glycaemic test within a few weeks.  So if there is a negative test within the month WITHOUT treatment (or indeed other evidence of diabetes), then you will ignore the first test

```{r}
second_earliest_dodgy_single <- single(dodgy_gly_next_earliest) %>% 
  select(patid, gly_date_adjusted) %>% 
  left_join(diagnostic_gly_obs, by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(obsdate>gly_date_adjusted) %>% 
    mutate(priority = if_else(hba1c==1, 1, 2)) %>%
    group_by(patid) %>% 
  filter(obsdate == min(obsdate)) %>% 
  arrange(priority, index) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(next_gly_date = obsdate,
         next_gly_term = Term) %>% 
mutate(next_gly_date = if_else((hba1c == 1 & (value < 6.5 | value > 20 & value < 48))|
                                 (is.na(hba1c) & !is.na(uln) & value < uln), next_gly_date, NA))

second_earliest_dodgy_multiple <- multiple(dodgy_gly_next_earliest) %>% 
  select(individual_id, gly_date_adjusted) %>% #expect many to many
  fill_columns() %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  left_join(diagnostic_gly_obs %>% select(patid, obsdate, Term, value, hba1c, index, uln), by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(obsdate>gly_date_adjusted) %>% 
    mutate(priority = if_else(hba1c==1, 1, 2)) %>%
    group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  filter(obsdate == min(obsdate)) %>% 
  arrange(priority, index) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(next_gly_date = obsdate,
         next_gly_term = Term) %>% 
mutate(next_gly_date = if_else((hba1c == 1 & (value < 6.5 | value > 20 & value < 48))|
                                 (is.na(hba1c) & !is.na(uln) & value < uln), next_gly_date, NA))%>% 
  select(-patid) %>% 
  fill_columns()
```

now for those that aren't dodgy
```{r}
second_earliest_single <- single(normo) %>% 
  filter(!patid %in% dodgy_gly$patid) %>% 
  left_join(first_update1 %>% select(patid, gly_date), by = "patid") %>% 
    mutate(priority = if_else(hba1c==1, 1, 2)) %>%
    group_by(patid) %>% 
  filter(obsdate == min(obsdate)) %>% 
  arrange(priority, index) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(next_gly_date = obsdate,
         next_gly_term = Term) %>% 
mutate(next_gly_date = if_else((hba1c == 1 & (value < 6.5 | value > 20 & value < 48))|
                                 (is.na(hba1c) & !is.na(uln) & value < uln), next_gly_date, NA)) %>% #now only keep those potentially that NEGATE diabetes
  mutate(next_gly_date = if_else(is.na(hba1c) & !is.na(uln) & value < uln, next_gly_date, NA))

second_earliest_multiple <- multiple(normo) %>% 
  filter(!individual_id %in% dodgy_gly$individual_id) %>% 
  left_join(first_update1 %>% select(patid, gly_date), by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(obsdate>gly_date) %>% 
    mutate(priority = if_else(hba1c==1, 1, 2)) %>%
    group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  filter(obsdate == min(obsdate)) %>% 
  arrange(priority, index) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(next_gly_date = obsdate,
         next_gly_term = Term) %>% 
mutate(next_gly_date = if_else((hba1c == 1 & (value < 6.5 | value > 20 & value < 48))|
                                 (is.na(hba1c) & !is.na(uln) & value < uln), next_gly_date, NA)) %>% #now only keep those that NEGATE diabetes
  select(-patid) %>% 
  fill_columns()
```
put them all together for the join
```{r}
second_earliest <- bind_rows(second_earliest_dodgy_single %>% select(patid, next_gly_date, next_gly_term), second_earliest_dodgy_multiple%>% select(patid, next_gly_date, next_gly_term), second_earliest_single%>% select(patid, next_gly_date, next_gly_term), second_earliest_multiple%>% select(patid, next_gly_date, next_gly_term))
```

lost patient - ie did not have a reliable next earliest gly date

```{r}
lost_patid <- dodgy_gly %>% 
  filter(!patid %in% dodgy_gly_next_earliest$patid)
```

only one diagnostic test for that patient and looks dodgy so need to
remove

#now for update 2, join on the ammended dates and amend the original
ones where necessary and remove the date for the lost patid

```{r}
first_update2 <- first_update1  %>% 
  left_join(dodgy_gly_next_earliest %>% select(patid, gly_date_adjusted, gly_term_adjusted, value_adjusted), by = "patid") %>% 
  mutate(gly_date = if_else(!is.na(gly_date_adjusted), gly_date_adjusted, gly_date),
         gly_term = if_else(!is.na(gly_term_adjusted), gly_term_adjusted, gly_term),
         value = if_else(!is.na(value_adjusted), value_adjusted, value)) %>% 
  mutate(gly_term = if_else(patid %in% lost_patid$patid, NA, gly_term),#for the lost patient, remove their value, gly date and gly test
         gly_date = if_else(patid %in% lost_patid$patid, NA, gly_date),
         value = if_else(patid %in% lost_patid$patid, NA, value)) %>% 
  left_join(second_earliest%>% select(patid, next_gly_date, next_gly_term), by = "patid") #potentially useful to have date when it looks like there is NOT DM
```
#Now look at likely erroneous first issuedates for update3,
pick those whose issuedate was in or before their year of birth
```{r}
dodgy_issuedate <- first_update2 %>% 
  filter(year(issuedate)<=yob) %>%
  select(patid, yob)
```

now get all the drugs of those subjects

```{r}
dodgy_issuedate_drugs<- all_dm_drugs %>% 
  inner_join(dodgy_issuedate %>% select(patid), by = "patid")
```

filter off date that is dodgy and find the next unique one to use for
adjustment

```{r}
dodgy_issuedate_next_date <- dodgy_issuedate_drugs %>% 
  filter(year(issuedate)>yob) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  filter(issuedate==min(issuedate)) %>% 
    ungroup() %>% 
distinct() %>% 
  mutate(prioritise_score = case_when(
    !is.na(priority_1)~1,
    !is.na(priority_2)~2,
    TRUE~3
  )) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>%
  filter(prioritise_score == min(prioritise_score)) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(updated_issuedate=issuedate) %>% 
  rename(updated_productname=productname) %>% 
  select(patid, updated_issuedate, updated_productname)
```

Note some patids may not have a valid issuedate - they need to be identifies so that their issuedate is removed in first_update3
```{r}
lost_patids <- dodgy_issuedate %>% 
  filter(!patid %in% dodgy_issuedate_next_date$patid)
```

##UPDATE 3

```{r}
first_update3 <- first_update2 %>% 
  left_join(dodgy_issuedate_next_date %>% select(patid, updated_issuedate, updated_productname), by = "patid") %>% 
  mutate(issuedate = coalesce(updated_issuedate, issuedate),
         productname = coalesce(updated_productname, productname)) %>% 
    mutate(issuedate = if_else(patid %in% lost_patids$patid, as.Date(NA), issuedate),
         productname = if_else(patid %in% lost_patids$patid, NA, productname))

n_distinct(filtered$individual_id)
```

next check if there are any silly HES dates - in our case there were none to update as the only
patient will be excluded anyway because the diabetes diagnosis date based on other evidence is before the entry window

```{r}
dodgy_hes_apc <-first_update3 %>% 
  filter(year(admidate)<=yob) #only 1 such person, type 1 dm and will be exlcuded as other dates before 2007 anyway so futile to try to update HES
```


#now filter to pats that have metformin alone as evidence of diabetes
These will be treated as per the algorithm for those with medication prescriptions as the only evidence of DM

```{r}

metformin_alone_single <- single(first_update3) %>% 
  inner_join(metformin_code %>% select(-priority_1, -priority_2, -prodcodeid), by = "productname") %>% 
  filter(is.na(gly_date)) %>% 
  filter(is.na(ddd)) %>% 
  filter(is.na(admidate)) %>% 
  select(patid)

metformin_alone_multiple <- multiple(first_update3) %>% 
  inner_join(metformin_code  %>%  select(-priority_1, -priority_2, -prodcodeid) , by = "productname") %>% 
  group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  filter(all(is.na(gly_date))) %>% 
  filter(all(is.na(ddd))) %>% 
  filter(all(is.na(admidate))) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  distinct(individual_id)

```

now pull their drugs up to and including the end of the entry window.  To be included in the cohort a subject has to have more than just metformin as evidence of diabetes during the entry window

```{r}
metformin_alone_all_drugs_single <- all_dm_drugs %>% 
  select(-individual_id) %>% #unnecessary column in those with single patids
  inner_join(metformin_alone_single, by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(year(issuedate)<2014 & year(issuedate)>yob)#need to just look at the entry windo

metformin_alone_all_drugs_multiple <- all_dm_drugs %>% 
  inner_join(metformin_alone_multiple, by = "individual_id") %>% 
    filter(year(issuedate)<2014 & year(issuedate)>yob)
```

 look at subjects that have nothing other than metformin - THESE ARE FOR EXCLUSION

```{r}
really_just_metformin_single <- metformin_alone_all_drugs_single %>%
  group_by(patid) %>%
  filter(all(is.na(priority_1))& all(is.na(priority_2))) %>% #filters out any patient that has even a single priority 1 or 2 drug
  ungroup() %>% 
  distinct(patid)

n_distinct(really_just_metformin_single$patid)

really_just_metformin_multiple <- multiple(metformin_alone_all_drugs_multiple) %>%
  group_by(individual_id) %>%
  filter(all(is.na(priority_1)) & all(is.na(priority_2))) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  distinct(individual_id, issuedate) %>% 
  group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  slice_min(issuedate) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  fill_columns(issuedate) %>% 
  distinct(patid, individual_id)

really_just_metformin <- bind_rows(really_just_metformin_multiple, really_just_metformin_single)
n_distinct(really_just_metformin_multiple$patid)
```
now create df of those that actually later have a priority drug.  Split into priority 1 and priority 2 as will deal with these differently as per metformin algorithm - ie a) if there is insulin and metformin AND PCOS AND GDM -> exclude  (more evidence of a diagnosis other than DM)
b) if there is insulin and metformin AND either PCOS or GDM -> wipe the metformin data and keep the insulin date (not we will later cross-reference with pregnancy)
c) if there is metformin and a priority_1 drug, this patient definitely has diabetes.  If they also have NDH or PCOS, wipe the metformin data and keep the priority_1 drug date as date of DM diagnosis.  If they have neither, keep the earliest prescription of any drug (and here it must be metformin because that is how we have selected the patients to examine above) as the date of diagnosis of diabetes as we have strong evidence of diabetes (the priority_1 drug) and no evidence of something else at this stage to explain the metformin - but again note we will later examine the overlap between the metformin scripts and pregnancy to ensure those scripts were not potentially explained by GDM.

Below we look at case A. I look at those with single patid IDs in more detail to ensure the validity of the approach (looking at years of different events) but for those with a multiple patid a shorter code is used for simplicity. There is also a little 'test' subset that subsets those being excluded who have a 'continuous' prescriptions; despite the continuous label it is clear that they still look like they should be excluded.  Also it is clear that in the excluded cohort there are fewer patids with conitunous scripts than in the total cohort
```{r}
insulin_met_single <-single(first_update3) %>% 
  filter(productname %in% insulin_code$productname|productname %in% metformin_code$productname) %>% 
  filter(is.na(gly_date) & is.na(admidate)& is.na(ddd) & (year(issuedate)<2014)) %>% #any issuedate after 2014 essentially irrelevant as will not influence ddd
  filter(!patid %in% really_just_metformin$patid) %>% 
  rename(original_issuedate = issuedate,
         original_prod = productname) %>% 
  select(patid, original_issuedate, original_prod, yob, individual_id, pattern) %>%
  filter(pattern!= "one-off") %>% #will be excluded anyway
left_join(all_dm_drugs %>% select(-yob, -individual_id), by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(year(issuedate)>yob) %>% #removes rubbish
  arrange(patid, issuedate) %>% 
  mutate(drug_year = year(issuedate)) %>% 
group_by(patid) %>% 
  filter(all(is.na(priority_1))) %>% 
  mutate(drug_years = list(unique(drug_year))) %>% 
slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  left_join(all_pcos_obs %>% select(patid, obsdate), by = "patid") %>% 
  arrange(patid, obsdate) %>% 
  mutate(pcos_year = year(obsdate)) %>% 
group_by(patid) %>% 
  mutate(pcos_years = list(unique(pcos_year))) %>% 
slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-obsdate) %>% 
  left_join(valid_gdm_obs_single %>%select(patid, obsdate), by = "patid") %>% 
  arrange(patid, obsdate) %>% 
  mutate(gdm_year = year(obsdate)) %>% 
group_by(patid) %>% 
  mutate(gdm_years = list(unique(gdm_year))) %>% 
slice(1) %>% 
ungroup() %>% 
  select(-priority_1, -priority_2, -index, -drug_year, -individual_id, -prodcodeid, -issuedate, -productname)

PCOS_GDM_exclude_single <- insulin_met_single %>% 
  filter(!is.na(pcos_years)&!is.na(gdm_years))

#same in multiple
PCOS_GDM_exclude_multiple <-multiple(first_update3) %>% 
  group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  filter(all(productname %in% insulin_code$productname)|all(productname %in% metformin_code$productname)) %>% 
  filter(all(is.na(gly_date)) & all(is.na(admidate)) & all(is.na(ddd))) %>%
  filter(!individual_id %in% really_just_metformin_multiple$individual_id) %>% 
  rename(original_issuedate = issuedate,
         original_prod = productname) %>% 
  select(patid, original_issuedate, original_prod, yob, individual_id, pattern) %>%
left_join(all_dm_drugs %>% select(-yob, -individual_id), by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(year(issuedate)>yob) %>% 
  group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  filter(all(is.na(priority_1))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(individual_id %in% valid_gdm_obs_multiple$individual_id & individual_id %in% all_pcos_obs$individual_id)

n_distinct(PCOS_GDM_exclude_multiple$individual_id)
```
Now looking at those who have not been excluded (ie have more than just metformin and don't have insulin + PCOS +GDM with no priority_1 drug).  If they have NDH or PCOS, we need to update to their priority drug.  If they have neither PCOS nor NDH we leave as is
```{r}
#this first bit of code to make metformin_then_priority_drug_single_priority is just used to examin the years of NDH with respect to the drug years
metformin_then_priority_drug_single_priority <- metformin_alone_all_drugs_single %>% 
  filter(!patid %in% really_just_metformin_single$patid & !patid %in% PCOS_GDM_exclude_single$patid) %>% 
  filter(patid %in% all_pcos_obs$patid|patid %in% ndh_obs$patid) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  summarise(drug_years = list(unique(year(issuedate))),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
    left_join(ndh_obs, by = "patid") %>% 
  left_join(insulin_met_single %>% select(patid, pcos_years), by = "patid")
  
#now create the df that will be used to update
drug_update_4_single <- metformin_alone_all_drugs_single %>% 
  filter(!patid %in% really_just_metformin_single$patid & !patid %in% PCOS_GDM_exclude_single$patid) %>% 
  filter(patid %in% all_pcos_obs$patid|patid %in% ndh_obs$patid) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(priority_1)| !is.na(priority_2)) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  slice_min(issuedate) %>%
      slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(u4_issuedate = issuedate,
         u4_productname = productname)

#note there are a very few patients in metformin alone who are neither in really just metformin, nor in PCOS GDM exclude, nor have PCOS or NDH

drug_update_4_multiple <- metformin_alone_all_drugs_multiple %>% 
  filter(!individual_id %in% really_just_metformin_multiple$patid & !individual_id %in% PCOS_GDM_exclude_multiple$individual_id) %>% 
    filter(individual_id %in% all_pcos_obs$individual_id|individual_id %in% ndh_obs$individual_id) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(priority_1)| !is.na(priority_2)) %>% 
    group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  slice_min(issuedate) %>%
      slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
    rename(u4_issuedate = issuedate,
         u4_productname = productname) %>% 
  select(-patid) %>% 
  fill_columns()

drug_update_4 <- bind_rows(drug_update_4_multiple, drug_update_4_single)
```

```{r}
#find first date of context-independant code
context_indep_date_single <- single(all_dm_obs) %>%

    group_by(patid) %>% 
  slice_min(obsdate) %>%

  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(context_indep_date = obsdate) %>% 
  left_join(first_update3 %>% select(patid, priority_date, admidate), by = "patid") %>%

  mutate(min_unequivocal_date = pmin(obsdate, context_indep_date, priority_date, admidate, na.rm = TRUE))

context_indep_date_multiple <- multiple(all_dm_obs) %>% 
  filter(is.na(context_dep)&is.na(possible_gdm)) %>% 
    group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  slice_min(obsdate) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-patid) %>% 
    rename(context_indep_date = obsdate) %>% 
    left_join(first_update3 %>% select(individual_id, patid, priority_date, admidate), by = "individual_id") %>% 
  left_join(hba1c_date_multiple %>% select(patid, obsdate), by = "patid") %>% 
  mutate(min_unequivocal_date = pmin(obsdate, context_indep_date, priority_date, admidate, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  summarise(obsdate = first(obsdate),
            min_unequivocal_date = min(min_unequivocal_date)) %>% 
  fill_columns()

context_indep_date <- bind_rows(context_indep_date_multiple, context_indep_date_single) %>% 
  select(patid, min_unequivocal_date, context_indep_date) 

#now create update 4

         metformin_exclude = if_else(patid %in% really_just_metformin$patid, 1, NA)
  ) %>% 
left_join(hba1c_date, by = "patid") %>% 
  left_join(context_indep_date, by = "patid") 

table(first_update4$metformin_exclude)
```

#now for update5 need to ensure that, if metformin prescription is driving the diabetes diagnosis date (ie issuedate = new_ddd),

we have already treated those in update 1 first identify those whose
first drug is metformin and who don't have any other evidence of

```{r}
  metformin_first_multiple <- multiple(first_update4) %>%
  group_by(individual_id) %>%

    min_ddd = safe_min(ddd),

         ddd_sans_met =pmin(min_gly, min_priority_date, min_ddd, min_admidate, na.rm=TRUE) ) %>% 
  filter(min_productname %in% metformin_code$productname) %>%
 filter(min_issuedate==new_ddd) %>%  #identify those whose ddd is driven by a drug prescription
    filter(min_issuedate %m+% years(1)< ddd_sans_met)
   #2751
  
metformin_first_multiple <- metformin_first_multiple%>%

metformin_first_single <- single(first_update4) %>%
```

#update 6 - ambiguous first observation codes
identify relevant patients - i.e. with a code potentially suggesting diabetes in pregnancy
```{r}
#makle a list of priority_1 drugs that are unambiguously used for DM
priority_1<- dm_drugs %>% 
  filter(!is.na(priority_1))

#identify subjects whose first diagnosis leaves ambiguity around whether it is GDM or DM
ambiguous_single <- single(first_update5) %>% 
  filter(grepl("pregnan", diagnosis, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  filter(!grepl("pre-existing", diagnosis, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% #note we should not include subjects with unambiguous 'pre-existing' diabetes in this ambiguous group
  filter(!grepl("pre-pregnancy counselling", diagnosis, ignore.case = TRUE)) #nor those who have DM and are receiving pre-pregnancy counseling, so those with "pre-existing" and "pre-pregnancy" are filtered out of the ambiguous group to really just leave the ambiguous first diagnoses

ambiguous_multiple <- multiple(first_update5) %>% 
  group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  filter(ddd==safe_min(ddd)) %>% #only look at those individuals whose earliest ddd is ambiguous, because we need to decide if that was an episode of GDM.  If it was a later episode then we assume it was DM all along
  filter(any(grepl("pregnan", diagnosis, ignore.case = TRUE))) %>% 
  filter(!any(grepl("pre-existing", diagnosis, ignore.case = TRUE))) %>% #note we should not include subjects with unambiguous 'pre-existing' diabetes in this ambiguous group....
  filter(!any(grepl("pre-pregnancy counselling", diagnosis, ignore.case = TRUE))) %>%  #nor those who have DM and are receiving pre-pregnancy counseling, so those with "pre-existing" and "pre-pregnancy" are filtered out of the ambiguous group to really just leave the ambiguous
ungroup() 
n_distinct(ambiguous_multiple$individual_id)

ambiguous_multiple_pats <- all_pats %>%    ##gives you number of patids involved
  filter(individual_id %in% ambiguous_multiple$individual_id)
```

filter out anyone with a useful HES data - i.e. an unambiguous HES term
or drug BEFORE or close to the CPRD term (you can then ignore the
ambiguous cprd diagnosis because it is predated by or close to something
unambiguous, but note some of the HES terms themselves are ambiguous and
are therefore labelled for review) an for those whose first HES code
could still be GDM (i.e. review flag 1), find next useful hes term if
there is one

```{r}
unambiguous_single <- ambiguous_single %>% 
  filter(admidate<=ddd %m+%years(1)|((productname %in% priority_1$productname) & issuedate<=ddd %m+% years(1)|hba1c_date<=ddd %m+% years(1))) %>% #any unequivocal evidence in year post partum searched
  select(patid, diagnosis, ddd, HES_term, admidate, individual_id, issuedate, productname, hba1c_date, value) 

unambiguous_multiple <- first_update5 %>% 
  filter(individual_id %in% ambiguous_multiple$individual_id) %>%
  group_by(individual_id) %>% 
    summarise(
    earliest_ddd = safe_min(ddd),
    earliest_admidate = safe_min(admidate),
    earliest_hba1c_date = safe_min(hba1c_date),
    # calculate earliest issuedate only among priority_1 drugs
    earliest_issuedate_priority = safe_min(issuedate[productname %in% priority_1$productname]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(earliest_admidate)&earliest_admidate <= earliest_ddd %m+% years(1) |
      !is.na(earliest_issuedate_priority)&earliest_issuedate_priority <= earliest_ddd %m+% years(1)|
      !is.na(earliest_hba1c_date)&earliest_hba1c_date <= earliest_ddd %m+% years(1)) %>% 
  ungroup()
#31

#remove these unambiguous patients from ambiguous
ambiguous_single <- ambiguous_single %>% 
  filter(!patid %in% unambiguous_single$patid)
  

ambiguous_multiple <- ambiguous_multiple %>% 
  filter(!individual_id %in% unambiguous_multiple$individual_id) 

true_ambiguous_multiple <- all_pats%>% 
  left_join(ambiguous_multiple%>% select(patid, ddd), by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(!individual_id %in% unambiguous_multiple$individual_id) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(individual_id)) %>%

#get a list of all the relevant patids

```
now find delivery dates for them as these will be needed compare any
events within the year following delivery (ie is this DM or GDM?)

```{r}
ambiguous_single$delivery_date <- NULL

rel_delivery_date_single <- ambiguous_single %>% 
  left_join(delivery_obs %>% select(patid, obsdate), by = "patid") %>%
  filter(!is.na(obsdate)) %>% 
  rename(delivery_date=obsdate) %>%   
  filter(delivery_date %m-% months(8)<=ddd) %>% 
  filter(delivery_date %m+% months(3)>=ddd) %>%
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  filter(delivery_date==min(delivery_date)) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() 


rel_delivery_date_multiple <- true_ambiguous_multiple %>% 
  left_join(delivery_obs %>% select(patid, obsdate), by = "patid") %>% 
  rename(delivery_date = obsdate) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(delivery_date)) %>%
  filter(delivery_date %m-% months(8)<=ddd) %>% 
  filter(delivery_date %m+% months(3)>=ddd) %>%  ##only select relevant episode as patients may have more than one delivery logged, allow a few months after delivery to allow for late coding
  group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  filter(delivery_date==min(delivery_date)) %>% #earliest relevant delivery date
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-patid) %>% 
  left_join(all_pats, by = "individual_id") %>%  ##now propagate to all related patids
  group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  fill(delivery_date, ddd, .direction = "downup") %>% 
  ungroup()

#we have some patients for whom we don't have a HES maternity date, seek it in CPRD
rel_delivery_date_to_find <- ambiguous_patients %>% 
  filter(!patid %in% rel_delivery_date_single$patid) %>% 
  filter(!patid %in% rel_delivery_date_multiple$patid)

```

So now we are left with some patids for whom we don't have a clear delivery date. In our case it was too large a number to sift through manually.  So look for a next diabetes observation within a year of the ambiguous observation and if there is one, you don't need a delivery date anyway because the ambiguous code is contiguous with an episode of chronic DM.

```{r}
 #identify individual for whome we need to find dm obsd
  rel_del_to_find_single <- single(rel_delivery_date_to_find)
 rel_del_to_find_multiple <- multiple(rel_delivery_date_to_find)

dm_obs_single <- all_dm_obs %>% 
  inner_join(rel_del_to_find_single %>% select(patid, ddd), by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(is.na(possible_gdm)) %>% #will lose some patients here
 filter(obsdate>ddd) %>% ##ensure no silly dates reappear, will also lose some patients here
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  mutate(priority = case_when(is.na(context_dep)&obsdate<=ddd%m+%years(1)~1, #for each patid, prioritise first any relevant codes within the year post ddd, then the minimum date
                              obsdate==min(obsdate)~2)) %>% 
  arrange(priority) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% #then keep, per patid, first the codes that clearly demonstrate dm (and are not context dependent) and then the minimum date
  mutate(cat = case_when(is.na(context_dep)&obsdate<=ddd%m+%years(1)~1, #this is DM
                           obsdate>ddd%m+%years(1)~2, ##this is GDM (and original DDD becomes GDD)
                           TRUE~3)) %>% # this remains ambiguous unless other useful info present
   ungroup()
 table(dm_obs_single$cat)
 

dm_obs_multiple <-  all_dm_obs %>% 
  inner_join(rel_del_to_find_multiple %>% select(patid, ddd), by = "patid") %>% #can use the patid as the key here as they are all present in rel_delivery to find  
  filter(is.na(possible_gdm)) %>% 
 filter(obsdate>ddd) %>% ##ensure no silly dates reappear
  group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  mutate(priority = case_when(is.na(context_dep)&obsdate<=ddd%m+%years(1)~1, #for each patid, prioritise first any relevant codes within the year post ddd, then the minimum date
                              obsdate==safe_min(obsdate)~2)) %>% 
  arrange(priority) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% #then keep, per patid, first the codes that clearly demonstrate dm (and are not context dependent) and then the minimum date
    mutate(cat = case_when(is.na(context_dep)&obsdate<=ddd%m+%years(1)~1, #this is DM
                           obsdate>ddd+years(1)~2, ##this is GDM (and original DDD becomes GDD - gestational diabetes date)
                           TRUE~3)) %>% # this remains ambiguous unless other useful info present
 arrange(cat) %>% 
 slice(1) %>% 
   ungroup() %>% 
   select(-patid) %>% 
  fill_columns(obsdate, Term)

    table(dm_obs_multiple$cat)
    
```

now need to make a df with all the delivery dates - we have 
explicit date,some implicit dates, and then we have to use the original
DDD of the ambiguous diagnosis ('diabetes in pregnancy') as a proxy for all other subjects (including those in ambiguous_del_dates) apart from those we know to have a subsequent unambiguous DM code within a year and therefore that original ambiguous code should be used as the DDD, so don't need to search for those 48 patids

```{r}
unambiguous_DM <- bind_rows(dm_obs_multiple, dm_obs_single) %>% 
  filter(cat==1)

all_del_dates <- bind_rows(rel_delivery_date_single, rel_delivery_date_multiple, ambiguous_del_date) %>% 
  select(patid, delivery_date)

remaining_ambiguous1 <- ambiguous_patients %>%

  group_by(patid) %>% #(note there are a few patients with multiple delivery dates an only a couple with multiple patids, looking at the data, all their patids have all the del dates so you can just gorup by patid)
  slice_min(delivery_date) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup()

n_distinct(remaining_ambiguous1$patid)
```

for the those patids with ambiguous first codes either you have another UNEQUIVOCAL dm
diagnosis within a year post-partum associated with that ambiguous initial date, or a medication or glycaemic test before
pregnancy or within a year of delivery → then you keep that ddd (
subjects) OR you have evidence later than a year → the previous ddd
becomes gdd and then use the next date as the ddd OR you don’t other
evidence → these are the lost_patients most of whom will be excluded as no evidence of diabetes and this is probably just
GDM (see below, those with an admidate do remain though)

1.  get all the dm diagnosis for these subjects, and keep their ddd
    because then you can compare each obsdate to the ddd to see whether
    it is within a year (then keep initial ddd), later than a year (then
    that inital ddd becomes the date of a gestational diabetes episode
    and the patient goes into the gdd cohort) or there is none at all
    (discard as no good evidence of pre-gestational diabetes).

```{r}
   inner_join(remaining_ambiguous3%>% select(patid, delivery_date), by = "patid")
```

now filter down to first unequivocal row, and prioritise to use the row
with the most useful info if there are two possible rows on that day

```{r}
ambiguous_dm_obs_first_unambiguous_single <- single(ambiguous_dm_obs) %>% 
  filter(is.na(possible_gdm)&is.na(context_dep)) %>% #ensure unequivocal codes
  mutate(                ####back date obs as appropriated
      adjusted_ddd = case_when(
      twelve_month_rev==1~obsdate %m-% months(12),
      six_month==1~obsdate %m-% months(6),
      three_month==1~obsdate %m-% months(3),
      TRUE~obsdate
    )) %>% 
filter(adjusted_ddd>delivery_date) %>% ##ensure no silly dates reappear
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  filter(adjusted_ddd==min(adjusted_ddd)) %>% 
  ungroup()

prioritise_single_fun <- function(df){
  df %>% 
    group_by(patid) %>% 
    slice(
      if(any(!is.na(twelve_month_rev))){
        which(!is.na(twelve_month_rev))[1]
      }else if(any(!is.na(six_month))){
        which(!is.na(six_month))[1]
      }else if(any(!is.na(three_month))) {
        which(!is.na(three_month))[1]
      }else{
        1
      }
    )
}
ambiguous_dm_obs_first_unambiguous_single <-prioritise_single_fun(ambiguous_dm_obs_first_unambiguous_single)
n_distinct(ambiguous_dm_obs_first_unambiguous_single$patid)

  
ambiguous_dm_obs_first_unambiguous_multiple <- multiple(ambiguous_dm_obs) %>%
  filter(is.na(possible_gdm) &is.na(context_dep)) %>% #ensure unequivocal codes
  mutate(                ####back date obs as appropriated
      adjusted_ddd = case_when(
      twelve_month_rev==1~obsdate %m-% months(12),
      six_month==1~obsdate %m-% months(6),
      three_month==1~obsdate %m-% months(3),
      TRUE~obsdate
    )) %>% 
filter(adjusted_ddd>delivery_date) %>% ##ensure no silly dates reappear
  group_by(individual_id) %>% 
  filter(adjusted_ddd==safe_min(adjusted_ddd)) %>% 
  ungroup()

prioritise_multiple_fun <- function(df){
  df %>% 
    group_by(individual_id) %>% 
    slice(
      if(any(!is.na(twelve_month_rev))){
        which(!is.na(twelve_month_rev))[1]
      }else if(any(!is.na(six_month))){
        which(!is.na(six_month))[1]
      }else if(any(!is.na(three_month))) {
        which(!is.na(three_month))[1]
      }else{
        1
      }
    )
}

ambiguous_dm_obs_first_unambiguous_multiple <-prioritise_multiple_fun(ambiguous_dm_obs_first_unambiguous_multiple) %>% 
  select(-patid) %>% 
  fill_columns(adjusted_ddd, Term)

#now build the total df of subjects whose initial ambiguous diagnosis may have related to a gdm episode AND they have later evidence of diabetes
GDM_pats <- bind_rows(ambiguous_dm_obs_first_unambiguous_multiple %>% select(patid, individual_id, adjusted_ddd, Term, delivery_date), ambiguous_dm_obs_first_unambiguous_single %>% select(patid, individual_id, adjusted_ddd, Term, delivery_date))
```


Now need to find lost patids - i.e. they were not filtered out of the
initial ambiguous cohort on account of having other evidence of diabetes
within the year and they were not found to have a later observation of
diabetes. For subjects in this category, unless they have a later
diagnostic test or a later drug, they are to be excluded as they only
have evidence of GDM. Below is the code to label them for exclusion if
they just have GDM or as patients for our GDM cohort. For those in the
GDM cohort we need to remove the diagnostic observation of the
ambiguous code because it should not be used to calculate the DDD (as it
relates to an episode of GDM) - these guys don't have a helpful later
diagnosis and need to be excluded as GDM only UNLESS they have other
evidence of diabetes from a drug post-partum or an admidate

```{r}
lost_patients <- remaining_ambiguous3%>% 
  filter(!patid %in% GDM_pats$patid) %>% 
  left_join(first_update5 %>% select(patid, diagnosis, gly_date, gly_term, hba1c_date, value, issuedate, productname, pattern, admidate, HES_term, pattern, years, context_indep_date), by = "patid") 

keep_ddd <- lost_patients %>%
  filter(
    # gly_date prior to 9 months before or 1 year after delivery
    (gly_date < delivery_date %m-% months(9)) |
    (gly_date > delivery_date & gly_date < delivery_date %m+% years(1)) |
   
    # issuedate prior 9 months before or 1 year after delivery
    (issuedate < delivery_date %m-% months(9)) |
    (issuedate > delivery_date & issuedate < delivery_date %m+% years(1)) |
   
    # admidate prior to 1 year after delivery
   admidate <= delivery_date %m+% years(1)|(productname %in% priority_1$productname & issuedate <= delivery_date %m-% years(1))
  ) %>% 
  select(-individual_id)
##few patids, none who have solid evidence of DM so we need to remove the ddd for ALL the lost patids

to_examin <- all_dm_obs %>% 
  filter(patid %in% lost_patients$patid)


```

Now these lost patients have no useful diagnosis after the initial
ambiguous diagnosis and none of the data in the dataframe suggests
there was either incontrovertible evidence of diabetes (through a hes
diagnosis or an unambiguous DM drug) within a year or that there was evidence of
metformin/insulin/hyperglycaemia OUTSIDE of pregnancy (either before or
within a year after delivery) suggesting the ambiguous diagnosis was
actually chronic DM. So we are left with a few case 
1) there is no other evidence at all of diabetes - GDM exclude 
2) there is glycaemic evidence of diabetes - a) during the pregnancy - need to update to the later
date. If none available than remove that glycamic code during pregnancy
b) more than a year after pregnancy - that is suggestive of chronic
diabetes UNLESS it is in the context of a pregnancy, at which point you
look for the next hyperglycaemia or if there is none, remove that
glycaemic code, and so on 
3) there is a prescription a) it is a priority
1 drug - keep patient in GDM cohort by virtue of the ambiguous
diagnosis b) it metformin/insulin and i) it is a one off - GDM exclude
UNLESS they have other evidence of diabetes (eg admidate) - if you look
at the one-offs, they are generally around the time of the ambiguous
diagnosis and may have been scripts given for GDM ii) it is
episodic/there is a gap - examine the years of prescription against the
pregnancy dates - most of these will be excluded, some need an update
when there is a prescription outside of pregnancy iii) it is
continuous - keep date and patient is in GDM cohort by virtue of the
ambiguous diagnosis 
4) there is an admidate - keep that date and patient
is in GDM cohort by virtue of the ambiguous diagnosis

```{r}
#now get the relevant dates for the GDM episodes
overlap_lost_single <- single(lost_patients) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(issuedate)) %>% 
  distinct(patid) %>% 
  left_join(all_dm_drugs %>% select(patid, issuedate, productname), by = "patid") %>%
  mutate(equivocal_years = year(issuedate)) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>%
  summarise(
    equivocal_years = list(unique(equivocal_years))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  left_join(all_pregnancy_obs_update %>% select(patid, obsdate, Term), by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(obsdate)) %>% 
  mutate(
    pregnancy_year = year(obsdate),
    pregnancy_month = month(obsdate)) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(
    match_year = list(if(pregnancy_month <= 6) c(pregnancy_year, pregnancy_year - 1) else pregnancy_year)) %>% 
  ungroup()

#and see if they all match up during the period of interest (ie issuedate to min_equivocal_date)
overlap_lost_single2 <- overlap_lost_single %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>%
  summarise(equivocal_years = list(sort(unique(unlist(equivocal_years)))),
            pregnancy_years = list(sort(unique(unlist(match_year)))),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  mutate(
    all_years_matched = mapply(function(p, g)  {
      presc <- as.integer(unlist(p))
      gdm <- as.integer(unlist(g))
      length(presc) > 0 &&
        all(presc %in% gdm)
    }, equivocal_years, pregnancy_years
    )) %>%
  ungroup()
table(overlap_lost_single2$all_years_matched)


#get the earliest year for which there is not a match with pregnancy
overlap_lost_single_update <- overlap_lost_single2 %>%
  filter(!all_years_matched) %>% 
  distinct(patid, pregnancy_years) %>% 
  unnest(pregnancy_years) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  mutate(pregnancy_number = row_number()) %>% 
   pivot_wider(
    names_from = pregnancy_number,
    values_from = pregnancy_years,
    names_prefix = "pregnancy_year_"
  ) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  left_join(overlap_lost_single2 %>% select(patid, equivocal_years), by = "patid") %>% 
  unnest(equivocal_years) %>%
  mutate(equivocal_years = as.numeric(equivocal_years)) %>% 
  filter(!if_any(starts_with("pregnancy_year_"), ~coalesce(.x == equivocal_years, FALSE))) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  slice_min(equivocal_years) %>% 
  filter(equivocal_years>2006 &equivocal_years<2014) %>% ##only check years that matter
  left_join(all_dm_drug_patterns %>% select(patid, pattern), by = "patid") %>% 
  left_join(all_pcos_obs, by = "patid")
#3 patids

drugs_to_examin <-  all_dm_drugs %>% filter(patid %in% overlap_lost_single_update$patid)

#now do the same for those with multiple IDs 
overlap_lost_multiple <- multiple(lost_patients) %>%
  filter(!is.na(issuedate)) %>% 
  distinct(individual_id) %>% 
  left_join(all_dm_drugs %>% select(individual_id, issuedate, productname), by = "individual_id") %>%
  mutate(equivocal_years = year(issuedate)) %>% 
  group_by(individual_id) %>%
  summarise(
    equivocal_years = list(unique(equivocal_years))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  left_join(all_pregnancy_obs_update %>% select(individual_id, obsdate, Term), by = "individual_id") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(obsdate)) %>% 
  mutate(
    pregnancy_year = year(obsdate),
    pregnancy_month = month(obsdate)) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(
    match_year = list(if(pregnancy_month <= 6) c(pregnancy_year, pregnancy_year - 1) else pregnancy_year)) %>% 
  ungroup()

#and see if they all match up during the period of interest (ie issuedate to min_equivocal_date)
overlap_lost_multiple2 <- overlap_lost_multiple %>%

  summarise(equivocal_years = list(sort(unique(unlist(equivocal_years)))),
```

examining this data from overlap_lost_, we can remove the all the medicatiosn in our case as they are either concomittent with a PCOS episode or they are out of the window anyway (or the records clearly state GDM, or it's just a single drug prescription out of the window/just metformin, which we exclude as too ambiguous)

Examination of the records here (looking at pregnancy data and also PCOS
records) shows there is no useful drug prescription and within diagnosis
window, clearly outside of pregnancy/PCOS prescription, therefore we
need to remove the drug for all of them apart from 11505569121901

so in total we can remove all drugs from lost_patients 

now look at glycaemia data

```{r}
overlap_gly_lost_single <- single(lost_patients) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(gly_date)) %>%  ##filter down to subjects that have glycaemic data
  select(-value) %>%               ##remove unnecessary vestigial value colum
  left_join(diagnostic_gly_obs, by = "patid") %>%  ##graft on glycaemic data
  mutate(gly_year = year(obsdate)) %>%   ##get the year of each observation
  group_by(patid) %>%
  summarise(
```

Examination of these records shows that there are clear glycaemic dates outside of pregnancy in 4 single patids HOWEVER actually it is just a single glucose outside of pregnancy so does not consititute diabetes

Now we have subjects from dm_obs dfs and 506 from next df obs - these don't need to
be touched - then GDM pats, for whom we have to update the ddd - all the rest are GDM exclude 

And now for update 6 -
need to left_join lost_ambiguous and adjusted_ambiguous to first_update5

```{r}
first_update6 <- first_update5 %>% 
  mutate(ambiguous_code = if_else(patid %in% ambiguous_single$patid | patid %in% ambiguous_multiple_pats$patid, 1, NA)) %>%   ##useful to have a record for later
  left_join(GDM_pats, by = "patid") %>% 
  mutate(gdd = case_when(patid %in% GDM_pats$patid ~ ddd,
                         TRUE~as.Date(NA)),
         gdm_status= case_when(patid %in% GDM_pats$patid ~ "GDM",
                         TRUE~NA),
        ddd = case_when(patid %in% GDM_pats$patid ~ gdm_adjusted_ddd,
                        patid %in% lost_patients$patid ~ as.Date(NA), 
                         TRUE~ddd),
         diagnosis= case_when(patid %in% GDM_pats$patid ~ gdm_adjusted_diag,
                         TRUE~diagnosis),  #chose not to remove the ambiguous term from the lost_patients for the record
         gly_date = case_when(patid %in% GDM_pats$patid ~ gdm_adjusted_gly_date,
                         patid %in% lost_patients$patid ~ as.Date(NA),
                         TRUE~gly_date),
         gly_term = case_when(patid %in% GDM_pats$patid ~ gdm_adjusted_gly_term,
                         patid %in% lost_patients$patid ~ NA,
                         TRUE~gly_term),
         value = case_when(patid %in% GDM_pats$patid ~ gdm_adjusted_value,
                         patid %in% lost_patients$patid ~ NA,
                         TRUE~value),
         issuedate = case_when(patid %in% GDM_pats$patid ~ gdm_adjusted_issuedate,
                         patid %in% lost_patients$patid ~ as.Date(NA),
                         pattern=="one-off" & is.na(gly_date) & is.na(admidate) & is.na(ddd) ~as.Date(NA),
                         TRUE~issuedate),
         productname = case_when(patid %in% GDM_pats$patid ~ gdm_adjusted_prod,
                         patid %in% lost_patients$patid ~ NA,
                         pattern=="one-off" & is.na(gly_date) & is.na(admidate) & is.na(ddd) ~ NA,
                         TRUE~productname)) %>% 
  left_join(context_dep_code, by = "diagnosis") %>% 
    mutate(equivocal_date = case_when(is.na(priority_date) & is.na(context_dep)~ pmin(issuedate, gly_date, na.rm=TRUE), ##use the issuedate and the gly date if the issuedate is not for a priority_1 drug
                                    is.na(priority_date) & !is.na(context_dep)~ pmin(ddd, issuedate, gly_date, na.rm=TRUE),#also used the ddd if it is a context dependant code
                                    !is.na(priority_date) &(priority_date==issuedate) & is.na(context_dep)~ pmin(ddd,gly_date, na.rm=TRUE),
                                    TRUE~gly_date)) # otherwise just use the gly date
```

#for update 7 we need to rule out context-dependent codes being related to GDM episodes
identify subjects with a context-dependent code prior to unequivocal evidence of DM by at least a year and who don't have any glycaemic or drug data within the year post-partum (which would otherwise indicate ongoing diabetes) 
```{r}
#first find those subjects whose context dependant code is before incontrevertible evidence of dm
context_dep_single <-single(first_update6) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(context_dep)) %>% 
  filter((ddd<min_unequivocal_date%m-%years(1))| is.na(min_unequivocal_date)) %>% 
  filter(year(ddd)<2014 & (year(min_unequivocal_date)>2006| is.na(min_unequivocal_date))) %>% #no point in looking at codes that will not influence a useful diagnosis
   select(patid, ddd, diagnosis, gly_date, issuedate, productname, admidate, HES_term, min_unequivocal_date, context_indep_date) 
  n_distinct(context_dep_single$patid)

```

first step of algorithm is to identify subjects with a context dependant code and no unequivocal diagnosis code nor glycamic test data nor admidate nor issuedate, then next step for the remaining look at whether the code was in pregnancy.  If they have any such codes, do not use a context dependant code to diagnose pregnancy 
```{r}
to_exclude_single <- context_dep_single %>% 
  filter(is.na(min_unequivocal_date) & is.na(gly_date) &is.na(issuedate))

overlap_context_single <- context_dep_single %>% 
  filter(!patid %in% to_exclude_single$patid) %>% 
  left_join(all_dm_obs %>% select(patid, obsdate, Term), by = "patid") %>%
  filter(obsdate<=context_indep_date %m-%years(1) |is.na(context_indep_date)) %>% ##just look at context-dependant observations prior to strong evidence of DM or where there is no such evidence of DM
  mutate(equivocal_years = year(obsdate)) %>% 
  filter(equivocal_years<2014) %>% #no point in updating later data
  group_by(patid) %>%
  summarise(
    equivocal_years = list(unique(equivocal_years))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  left_join(all_pregnancy_obs_update %>% select(patid, obsdate, Term), by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(obsdate<as.Date("2015-01-01")) %>% #overlap with relevant pregnancy years
  mutate(
    pregnancy_year = year(obsdate),
    pregnancy_month = month(obsdate)) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(
  match_year = list(if(pregnancy_month <= 6) c(pregnancy_year, pregnancy_year - 1) else pregnancy_year)) %>% 
  ungroup()

n_distinct(overlap_context_single$patid)

filtered_out_single <- context_dep_single %>% 
  filter(!patid %in% to_exclude_single$patid) %>% 
  filter(!patid %in% overlap_context_single$patid) %>% #note here we are looking for those not in overlap_context dep as they for example have context dep code is >=2014 so not worth amending
  select(-min_unequivocal_date)


#and see if they all match up during the period of interest create variable all_years_matched which is a boolean describing whether all the years of context dep codes are explained by pregnancy epsiodes
overlap_context_single2 <- overlap_context_single %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>%
  summarise(equivocal_years = list(sort(unique(unlist(equivocal_years)))),
            pregnancy_years = list(sort(unique(unlist(match_year)))),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  mutate(
    all_years_matched = mapply(function(c, g)  {
      context <- as.integer(unlist(c))
      gdm <- as.integer(unlist(g))
      length(context) > 0 &&
        all(context %in% gdm)
    }, equivocal_years, pregnancy_years
    )) %>%
  ungroup()

#subjects whom we should wipe all context dependant codes as all their years are matched
all_years_matched_single <- overlap_context_single2 %>% 
  filter(all_years_matched)
#...and find the next unambiguous observation for the update
all_years_matched_single_next <- all_dm_obs %>% 
  filter(patid %in% all_years_matched_single$patid) %>% 
  filter(is.na(context_dep)&is.na(possible_gdm)) %>% #just filter down to relevant context-independent codes
    mutate(                ####back date obs as appropriated
      adjusted_ddd = case_when(
      twelve_month_rev==1~obsdate %m-% months(12),
      six_month==1~obsdate %m-% months(6),
      three_month==1~obsdate %m-% months(3),
      TRUE~obsdate
    )) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  filter(adjusted_ddd==min(adjusted_ddd)) %>% 
    group_by(patid) %>% 
    slice(
      if(any(!is.na(twelve_month_rev))){
        which(!is.na(twelve_month_rev))[1]
      }else if(any(!is.na(six_month))){
        which(!is.na(six_month))[1]
      }else if(any(!is.na(three_month))) {
        which(!is.na(three_month))[1]
      }else{
        1
      }
    )%>% 
    rename(ddd_u7 = adjusted_ddd,
         diagnosis_u7 = Term)

#for those whose context dep codes all match pregnancy years - remove their ddd and diagnosis
remove_diag <-all_years_matched_single %>% 
  filter(all_years_matched) 

#for those with unmatched years, if the context dep code is before or up to a GDM episode (next step in the algorithm), remove all context dep codes
all_years_unmatched_single <- overlap_context_single2 %>% 
  filter(!all_years_matched) %>%
  left_join(first_update6 %>% select(patid,ddd, min_unequivocal_date), by = "patid") %>% 
  left_join(total_gdm_single_deliveries_slimmed, by = "patid") %>% #  
  mutate(true_gdm = if_else(gdm_del_date < min_unequivocal_date %m-% years(1)|(!is.na(gdm_del_date) &  is.na(min_unequivocal_date)), 1, NA)) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
    mutate(remove = if_else(any(ddd<gdm_del_date %m+% months(3) & !is.na(true_gdm)), 1, NA)) %>% ##allow a bit of leeway
  ungroup() 

#for those whose diagnosis we need to remove, we need to find the next diag that is not context dependant
all_years_unmatched_single_next <- all_years_unmatched_single %>% 
  filter(!is.na(remove)) %>%
  distinct(patid) %>% 
  left_join(all_dm_obs, by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(is.na(context_dep)&is.na(possible_gdm)) %>% 
    mutate(                ####back date obs as appropriated
      adjusted_ddd = case_when(
      twelve_month_rev==1~obsdate %m-% months(12),
      six_month==1~obsdate %m-% months(6),
      three_month==1~obsdate %m-% months(3),
      TRUE~obsdate
    )) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  filter(adjusted_ddd==min(adjusted_ddd)) %>% 
    slice(
      if(any(!is.na(twelve_month_rev))){
        which(!is.na(twelve_month_rev))[1]
      }else if(any(!is.na(six_month))){
        which(!is.na(six_month))[1]
      }else if(any(!is.na(three_month))) {
        which(!is.na(three_month))[1]
      }else{
        1
      }
    )%>% 
    rename(ddd_u7 = adjusted_ddd,
         diagnosis_u7 = Term)
  
#now identify those to take to next step of algorithm, i.e all their years don't match, and they are not prior to GDM
  for_next_step_single <- all_years_unmatched_single %>% 
  filter(is.na(remove)) %>% 
    bind_rows(.,filtered_out_single)#only keep those whose diagnosis you are not going to remove ??NOT NEEDED

table(all_years_unmatched_single$remove)

```

now look to see if there are large gaps in coding suggesting separate episodes
```{r}
large_gap_single <- all_dm_obs %>% 
  filter(patid %in% for_next_step_single$patid) %>%
  mutate(                ####back date obs as appropriated
    adjusted_ddd = case_when(
      twelve_month_rev==1~obsdate %m-% months(12),
      six_month==1~obsdate %m-% months(6),
      three_month==1~obsdate %m-% months(3),
      TRUE~obsdate
    )) %>% 
  left_join(first_update6 %>% select(patid, min_unequivocal_date, yob, gly_date, issuedate), by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(adjusted_ddd<min_unequivocal_date %m-% years(1) |is.na(min_unequivocal_date)) %>% #equivocal dates in the year prior to unequivocal data probably constitute the start of diabetes so we need to ignore them when looking for a gap to unequivocal evidence
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  slice_max(adjusted_ddd) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(dodgy = if_else(year(adjusted_ddd)<yob+50 & (adjusted_ddd < min_unequivocal_date%m-% years(2)), 1, NA)) ##identify those with a large gap
  
large_gap_single_no <-large_gap_single %>% 
  filter(is.na(dodgy)) %>%  
  distinct(patid, obsdate, yob) 

large_gap_single_yes<-large_gap_single%>% 
  filter(!is.na(dodgy)) %>% 
  distinct(patid, yob)
n_distinct(large_gap_single_yes$patid)

#for those with a large gap, update
large_gap_single_update <- large_gap_single_yes %>% 
  left_join(all_dm_obs, by = "patid") %>% 
    mutate(                ####back date obs as appropriated
    adjusted_ddd = case_when(
      twelve_month_rev==1~obsdate %m-% months(12),
      six_month==1~obsdate %m-% months(6),
      three_month==1~obsdate %m-% months(3),
      TRUE~obsdate
    )) %>% 
  filter(is.na(context_dep)&is.na(possible_gdm)) %>%
  filter(year(adjusted_ddd)>yob) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  slice_min(adjusted_ddd) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
    rename(ddd_u7 = adjusted_ddd,
         diagnosis_u7 = Term)
```

```{r}
      TRUE~obsdate
    )) %>% 
```
```{r}
  group_by(individual_id) %>% 
```
```{r}
  filter(adjusted_ddd==min(adjusted_ddd)) %>%

      }else if(any(!is.na(three_month))) {
        which(!is.na(three_month))[1]
      }else{
        1
      }
    )%>% 
    rename(ddd_u7 = adjusted_ddd,
         diagnosis_u7 = Term) %>% 
  select(-patid) %>% 
  fill_columns()
```

#now for update 7
- remove ddd and diagnosis with a context-dependant code either if there is a large gap or if it is in pregnancy and replace with a context indep code, if there is one.  Otherwise leave the context indep code
- note needs update are those with context indep codes and a pregnancy and to update contains those with a large gap as well as those with a pregnancy who HAVE a context indep code - so we need to remove the ddd and diagnoses for anyone featuring in either of these dfs and then replace them with context indep codes were possible
- we also label these subjects as possible GDM - not all of them have overt GDM coding but a lot do and the rest clearly have overlap with pregnancy or a large gap between context dep and context indep coding suggesting an episodic disease pattern like GDM. This label should be used in a SENSITIVITY analysis later in which they are all treated as being part of the GDM cohort (note many will also have clear evidence of GDM already but the sensitivity analysis will add these possible_GDMs into the GDM cohort too).
```{r}
##
first_update7 <- first_update6%>% 
  mutate(ddd = if_else(patid %in% remove_diags$patid, as.Date(NA), ddd),
         diagnosis = if_else(patid %in% remove_diags$patid, NA, diagnosis)) %>% 
  left_join(to_update, by = "patid") %>% 
  mutate(ddd = if_else(!is.na(ddd_u7), ddd_u7, ddd),
         diagnosis = if_else(!is.na(diagnosis_u7), diagnosis_u7, diagnosis),
         possible_gdm = if_else(patid %in% remove_diags$patid, 1, NA)) #log those with evidence of pregnancy at least as GDM subjects

```

ensure that those without a value in the diagnosis column, the HES_term column and without a priority 1 drug at any point do not just have GDM and that the script of metformin or insulin was not used for GDM (if so, need to adjust date), and run through update 4 to rule out PCOS again (necessary because some patients have lost their diagnoses in update 6, as it was only an ambiguous one)

```{r}
  filter(is.na(min_unequivocal_date)) %>%
  filter(is.na(ddd)) %>% ##ddd's should now be unquivocal too
  filter(is.na(gdm_status)) %>%  #no point searching patients that have already been labelled for exclusion by an ambiguous first diagnosis, and note any one in the GDM column has already been filtered out because they have a ddd
  filter(is.na(PCOS_GDM_exclude)&is.na(metformin_exclude)) %>% #no point searching through those already excluded by PCOS
  filter(!is.na(gly_date)|!is.na(issuedate)) %>%

   filter(all(is.na(min_unequivocal_date))) %>%

  filter(is.na(PCOS_GDM_exclude)&is.na(metformin_exclude)) %>%  #no point searching through those already excluded by PCOS
  group_by(individual_id) %>%
```

now can check for overlapping time periods with pregnancy

```{r}
#now get the relevant dates for the potential pregnancy episodes and drug years
overlap_single <- no_diagnosis_nor_hes_nor_priority1_single %>% 
  filter(!is.na(issuedate)) %>% 
  distinct(patid, issuedate) %>% 
  rename(old_issue = issuedate) %>% 
  left_join(all_dm_drugs %>% select(patid, issuedate, productname), by = "patid") %>%
  filter(issuedate>= old_issue) %>% ## necessary because of upstream updates
  mutate(equivocal_years = year(issuedate)) %>% 
  filter(equivocal_years<2014) %>% #no point in updating later data
  group_by(patid) %>%
  summarise(
    equivocal_years = list(unique(equivocal_years))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  left_join(all_pregnancy_obs_update %>% select(patid, obsdate, Term), by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(obsdate<as.Date("2015-01-01")) %>% 
  mutate(
    pregnancy_year = year(obsdate),
    pregnancy_month = month(obsdate)) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(
    match_year = list(if(pregnancy_month <= 6) c(pregnancy_year, pregnancy_year - 1) else pregnancy_year)) %>% 
  ungroup()

#and see if they all match up during the period of interest (ie issuedate to min_equivocal_date) - create variable all_years_matched which is a boolean describing whether all the years of drugs are explained by pregnancy epsiodes
overlap_single2 <- overlap_single %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>%
  summarise(equivocal_years = list(sort(unique(unlist(equivocal_years)))),
            pregnancy_years = list(sort(unique(unlist(match_year)))),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  mutate(
    all_years_matched = mapply(function(p, g)  {
      presc <- as.integer(unlist(p))
      gdm <- as.integer(unlist(g))
      length(presc) > 0 &&
        all(presc %in% gdm)
    }, equivocal_years, pregnancy_years
    )) %>%
  ungroup()

table(overlap_single2$all_years_matched)

#get the earliest year for which there is not a match with pregnancy for those whose drug prescription don't all match
overlap_single_update <- overlap_single2 %>%
  filter(!all_years_matched) %>% # subset those whose scripts don't all overlap with pregnancy
  distinct(patid, pregnancy_years) %>% 
    left_join(first_update7b %>% select(patid, gly_date, gly_term, hba1c_date), by = "patid") %>% 
  left_join(all_dm_drugs %>% select(patid, issuedate, prodcodeid, productname), by = "patid") %>% 
  filter(year(issuedate)<2014) %>% 
  mutate(metformin = if_else(prodcodeid %in% metformin_code$prodcodeid, 1, NA_real_)) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  mutate(metformin = if_else(all(metformin==1), 1, NA_real_),
         remove = if_else(metformin==1 & (is.na(gly_date)|year(gly_date)>2013), 1, NA)) %>% #insufficient evidence of diabetes
  ungroup() %>% 
  unnest(pregnancy_years) %>% 
  arrange(patid, pregnancy_years) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  mutate(pregnancy_number = row_number(),
         latest_pregnancy = if_else(pregnancy_number==max(pregnancy_number), pregnancy_years, NA_integer_)) %>%##find the latest pregnancy - useful to be able to compare drugs to latest pregnancy
  fill(latest_pregnancy, .direction = "downup") %>% 
  ungroup()

remove_metformin_single <- overlap_single_update %>% 
  filter(!is.na(remove)) %>% 
  distinct()

overlap_single_update2 <- overlap_single_update %>% 
  filter(is.na(remove)) %>% 
  distinct(patid, pregnancy_number, pregnancy_years, metformin, latest_pregnancy) %>%
  unnest(pregnancy_years) %>%  
  group_by(patid, latest_pregnancy) %>% 
   pivot_wider(
    names_from = pregnancy_number,
    values_from = pregnancy_years,
    names_prefix = "pregnancy_year_"
  ) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  left_join(overlap_single2 %>% select(patid, equivocal_years, pregnancy_years), by = "patid") %>% 
  unnest(equivocal_years) %>%
  mutate(equivocal_years = as.numeric(equivocal_years)) %>% 
  filter(!if_any(starts_with("pregnancy_year_"), ~coalesce(.x == equivocal_years, FALSE))) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  slice_min(equivocal_years) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(equivocal_years>2006 &equivocal_years<2014) %>% 
  select(patid, equivocal_years, pregnancy_years, metformin, latest_pregnancy) %>% 
  left_join(all_dm_drugs %>% select(patid, issuedate, productname, priority_1, priority_2, index), by = "patid") %>% 
  mutate(issueyear = year(issuedate)) %>% 
  filter(equivocal_years==issueyear) %>% #now start to look for the earliest unmatched year
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  filter(issuedate==min(issuedate)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(priority=case_when(!is.na(priority_1)~1,
                            !is.na(priority_2)~2,
                            TRUE~3)) %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  arrange(priority) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(unmatched_drug_update = issuedate) %>% 
  select(-priority_2, -index) %>% 
  left_join(gdm_obs %>% select(patid, obsdate), by = "patid") %>% 
  group_by(patid) %>% 
  slice_max(obsdate) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(issue_before_gdm = if_else(is.na(priority_1) & (unmatched_drug_update <=obsdate %m+% months(6)), 1L, NA_integer_), #if the medication is prior to GDM (and is either isulin or metformin), likely all GDM
         keep = if_else(equivocal_years>=latest_pregnancy +2, 1, NA_integer_)) #equivocal year is long after pregnancies so is probably fine to keep
```

In fact for those with multiple patids (24 patid, 12 individuals), those with unmatched dates did not have two convincingly separate dated glycaemic test dates (two individuals did have different dates, but they were max 3 days apart and it was the same test with the same value so probably just a trasncription issue from one patid to another). Therefore we can wipe all the glycaemic test data for all those in overlap_gly_multiple2

#NEXT ensure anyone whose obs we are going to wipe doesn't have other evidence to suggest we should be keeping the pregnancy evidence as actual first evidence of diam
look at discrepency between all years being matched in the period of interest between drugs and glycaemia - ie if we think everything is matched from drug perspective is it also from a glycaemic perspective during 2007-2013?  If so wipe all their data -> YES WIPE ALL

```{r}
#here we can simply compare drug data relevant to the delivery that is closest to the date being wipes
check_single<- overlap_gly_single2 %>% 
  filter(all_gly_years_matched) %>% 
  unnest(years) %>% #some rows have more than one year
  filter(years<2014) %>% 
  left_join(all_deliveries_single %>% select(patid, delivery_date), by = "patid") %>% #this is a bit blunt because I don't have a delivery for every pregnancy but it's good enough numbers-wise
  mutate(delivery_years= year(delivery_date)) %>% 
  filter(years >= delivery_years -1  & years<= delivery_years +1) %>% 
  left_join(all_dm_drugs %>% select(patid, issuedate, productname), by = "patid") %>% #expect many to many
  mutate(drug_year = year(issuedate)) %>% 
    filter(drug_year >= delivery_years -1) %>% 
filter(drug_year<= delivery_years +1) %>% 
  distinct(issuedate, delivery_years, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  select(-all_gly_years_matched)

to_examin_drugs <- all_dm_drugs %>% filter(patid %in% check_single$patid)
#nothing to recoup

  filter(all_gly_years_matched) %>%

  filter(years<2014) %>% 
  fill_columns() %>% 
  left_join(all_deliveries_multiple %>% select(patid, delivery_date), by = "patid") %>% #this is a bit blunt because I don't have a delivery for every pregnancy but it's good enough numbers-wise
  mutate(delivery_years= year(delivery_date)) %>% 
  filter(years >= delivery_years -1  & years<= delivery_years +1) %>% 
  left_join(all_dm_drugs, by = "patid") %>% #expect many to many

#nothing to recoup
```
